question: A laser is placed at the point \((3, 5).\) The laser beam travels in a straight line. Larry wants the beam to hit and bounce off the \(y\)-axis, then hit and bounce off the \(x\)-axis, then hit the point \((7, 5).\) What is the total distance the beam will travel along this path?
solution:
A reflection can straighten a bounce: equal incoming and outgoing angles make the reflected outgoing segment line up with the incoming segment. Reflections also preserve lengths.

Let \(L=(3,5)\) be the laser and \(T=(7,5)\) the target. Reflect the target across the axes in reverse order of the bounces. First reflect across the \(x\)-axis to obtain \(T'=(7,-5)\), then across the \(y\)-axis to obtain \(T''=(-7,-5)\). Unfolding the two bounces this way turns the beam's path into the straight segment \(LT''\), without changing its total length.

To check the bounce order, the line through \(L\) and \(T''\) is \(y=x+2\). Traveling from \(L\), it crosses the \(y\)-axis at \(P=(0,2)\), then the \(x\)-axis at \(Q'=(-2,0)\). Reflecting \(Q'\) across the \(y\)-axis gives the actual second bounce \(Q=(2,0)\). Thus folding the path back gives \(L\) to \(P\) to \(Q\) to \(T\), as required.

The total distance is therefore
\[
LT''=\sqrt{(3-(-7))^2+(5-(-5))^2}
=\sqrt{100+100}
=\boxed{10\sqrt2}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\text{C}\).
